mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an ADU and an in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: An accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is a secondary housing structure located on the same parcel of land as a primary single-family home. It must contain its own independent living facilities, including a dedicated kitchen, bathroom, sleeping area, and private entrance. In contrast, an in-law suite or guest room is often an interior bedroom conversion or home addition that still shares central utilities, entrances, or common kitchen spaces with the primary residence. Choosing between a full ADU and an attached guest suite depends largely on whether you need a fully autonomous home for multigenerational living or rental use, versus an accessible private bedroom integrated under the main roofline.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is a fully independent residential unit with its own kitchen, bath, and private entrance, whereas an in-law suite often shares living areas, kitchens, or entrances within the main house.
